name: Native sidecar containers
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. Native sidecar containers (GA 1.29): an initContainer with restartPolicy: Always that starts before the app, runs alongside it, and is torn down last — so it works correctly in Jobs (unlike a plain extra container that never exits). Build one, then fix a Job that a non-native sidecar keeps from completing.

questions.title: Add a native sidecar to a Deployment
questions.teach:
A **native sidecar** is an `initContainer` with `restartPolicy: Always`. It starts **before** the app containers, keeps running alongside them, and the kubelet restarts it if it dies. Unlike a plain extra container in `containers:`, a native sidecar has ordered startup and is guaranteed to terminate **after** the app containers.

**Gotcha:** the sidecar goes under `initContainers:` (not `containers:`) and MUST have `restartPolicy: Always` — without that field it's an ordinary init container that must exit before the app starts.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `sidecar-learn`, create a Deployment `web` (1 replica) whose app container is `app` (`nginx:1.25`) and that has a **native sidecar** init container `log-agent` (`busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 10; done'`) with `restartPolicy: Always`.

Target: Deployment `web` has 1 ready replica; its pod has an `initContainers` entry `log-agent` with `restartPolicy: Always`, and the `app` container running.
questions.hint: In the pod template put `initContainers: [{name: log-agent, image: busybox:1.36, restartPolicy: Always, command: [...]}]` alongside `containers: [{name: app, image: nginx:1.25}]`. The `restartPolicy: Always` on the initContainer is what makes it a sidecar.
questions.solution:
kubectl create namespace sidecar-learn 2>/dev/null
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: sidecar-learn
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: { matchLabels: { app: web } }
  template:
    metadata: { labels: { app: web } }
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: log-agent
        image: busybox:1.36
        restartPolicy: Always
        command: ["sh","-c","while true; do echo tick; sleep 10; done"]
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
YAML
kubectl -n sidecar-learn rollout status deploy/web

verification.description: Deployment web ready with native sidecar log-agent (initContainer restartPolicy Always)

questions.eli5:
Think of a Pod as a tiny food truck. The **app container** is the cook making burgers. A **sidecar** is a helper who stands next to the cook the whole shift — maybe they haul away the trash (ship the logs) or keep the grill lit. You want that helper to arrive **before** the cook starts, stick around **while** they cook, and leave **after** the cook clocks out.

A **native sidecar** is how Kubernetes hires that helper properly. You list the helper under `initContainers` (the "arrive early" list) but give it a special badge: `restartPolicy: Always`. That badge changes everything — instead of the helper doing one quick setup task and leaving (a normal init container), it stays on the whole shift and gets re-hired instantly if it ever collapses.

So the recipe is: helper (`log-agent`) goes in `initContainers` **with** `restartPolicy: Always`, and the cook (`app`, nginx) goes in the normal `containers` list. Kubernetes starts the helper, waits for it to be up, then starts the cook.

**Watch out for:**

- **The helper MUST go under `initContainers:`, not `containers:`.** If you put it in the normal `containers` list it's just a second app container, not a native sidecar.
- **`restartPolicy: Always` is the magic word.** Leave it off and you have an *ordinary* init container — Kubernetes will wait for it to **finish and exit** before starting the cook. A helper that loops forever (`while true`) never exits, so the app would never start.
- **Order matters:** native sidecars start *before* app containers and are torn down *after* them.
- This is a GA feature since Kubernetes **1.29** — on older clusters the field is ignored.
questions.deepDive: ## Native sidecar containers — full rundown ### The one-sentence model A **native sidecar** is an `initContainer` with `restartPolicy: Always`. It starts **before** the app containers, keeps **running alongside** them for the pod's whole life, and is **torn down after** the app containers finish. (GA in Kubernetes **1.29**.) ### Why it exists Before native sidecars, a "sidecar" was just a second entry in `containers:`. That works for a Deployment (runs forever anyway) but breaks two things: 1. **Startup ordering** — nothing guaranteed the log/proxy helper was ready before the app started. 2. **Jobs** — a Job's pod only completes when **all** `containers:` exit. A helper that loops forever keeps the pod `Running` and the Job **never completes**. Native sidecars fix both: ordered startup, and automatic teardown when the main containers finish. ### Where it goes ```yaml spec: initContainers: - name: log-agent image: busybox:1.36 restartPolicy: Always # <-- this field makes it a sidecar command: ["sh","-c","while true; do echo tick; sleep 10; done"] containers: - name: app image: nginx:1.25 ``` ### initContainer behavior by restartPolicy | `restartPolicy` on the initContainer | Behavior | |---|---| | *(unset)* | Ordinary init container — must **run to completion and exit** before app containers start. A forever-loop here = pod stuck in `Init`. | | `Always` | **Native sidecar** — starts, becomes Ready, app containers then start; sidecar keeps running; restarted if it dies; terminated last. | | `OnFailure` / `Never` | Invalid for this purpose — not a sidecar. | > Note: `restartPolicy` on an **individual initContainer** is a distinct field from the pod-level `spec.restartPolicy`. Only `Always` is meaningful here. ### Lifecycle ordering ``` start: initContainers (in order) ──► native sidecars become Ready ──► app containers start run: sidecars + app run together; kubelet restarts a crashed sidecar stop: app containers terminate ──► then native sidecars terminate ``` ### Startup / readiness - A native sidecar is considered "started" once it's running (and passes its `startupProbe` if set); only then do later containers proceed. - You can give a native sidecar its own `livenessProbe`, `readinessProbe`, `startupProbe`, `lifecycle` hooks, and `resources` — things ordinary init containers couldn't fully use. ### Create / inspect commands ```bash # apply from a manifest (recommended for the exam) kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml kubectl -n sidecar-learn rollout status deploy/web # confirm the sidecar is an initContainer with restartPolicy Always kubectl -n sidecar-learn get deploy web \ -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].restartPolicy}'; echo # -> Always # see both containers running in the pod kubectl -n sidecar-learn get pod -l app=web \ -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.initContainers[*].name} | {.items[0].spec.containers[*].name}'; echo ``` ### Gotchas & exam traps - **Wrong list.** Putting the sidecar in `containers:` instead of `initContainers:` makes it a plain app container — not a native sidecar, and no ordering/teardown guarantees. - **Missing `restartPolicy: Always`.** Without it, a looping helper under `initContainers:` traps the pod in `Init` forever (it never exits). - **`kubectl edit` can't add an initContainer to a running Pod** — pod spec is largely immutable. Edit the **Deployment** template and let it roll a new pod, or recreate the pod. - **Cluster version < 1.29** ignores the feature (older betas needed the `SidecarContainers` feature gate). CKA is on a current version, so assume GA. - The sidecar still **counts toward the pod's total resource requests** used for scheduling. ### Quick reference ```yaml spec: initContainers: - name: image: restartPolicy: Always # the only thing that makes it a sidecar command: [ ... ] # long-running containers: - name: image: ``` ```bash kubectl apply -f deploy.yaml kubectl -n rollout status deploy/ kubectl -n get deploy -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].restartPolicy}' ```

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a Job that never completes (sidecar)
questions.teach:
In a **Job**, a plain extra container that runs forever keeps the Pod alive, so the Job **never completes**. The fix is to make that helper a **native sidecar** (move it to `initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`): native sidecars are terminated automatically once the main containers finish, so the Job completes.

**Gotcha:** a Job's pod template is immutable — you can't edit the running Job's containers. Delete and recreate the Job with the sidecar as a native sidecar.
questions.prompt:
Setup created Job `batch-job` in `sidecar-learn` whose `worker` container does its work and exits, but a second plain container `helper` runs forever — so the Job never completes. Fix it so `batch-job` **completes**, keeping `helper` as a **native sidecar**.

Target: a Job `batch-job` in `sidecar-learn` reaches `Complete`, and its pod template runs `helper` as a native sidecar (initContainer with `restartPolicy: Always`).
questions.hint: `kubectl -n sidecar-learn delete job batch-job`, then recreate it with `worker` under `containers:` and `helper` moved to `initContainers:` with `restartPolicy: Always`. The worker exits → native sidecar is torn down → Job completes.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n sidecar-learn delete job batch-job --ignore-not-found
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: batch-job
  namespace: sidecar-learn
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      initContainers:
      - name: helper
        image: busybox:1.36
        restartPolicy: Always
        command: ["sh","-c","while true; do echo helping; sleep 5; done"]
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","echo working; sleep 5; echo done"]
YAML
kubectl -n sidecar-learn wait --for=condition=complete job/batch-job --timeout=90s

verification.description: Job batch-job Complete with helper as a native sidecar

questions.eli5:
Imagine a Job is a chore with a clear finish line: "wash the dishes, then you're done." The **worker** is the person washing dishes — they finish and sit down. But someone added a **helper** who's running the faucet and has been told "never stop running the faucet." So even though the dishes are done, the faucet is still going, and the chore is marked **"not finished yet"** forever. The room never empties, so the chore never gets checked off.

That's exactly what a plain forever-running helper container does inside a Job: a Job only counts as **Complete** when **all** its normal containers stop, and a `while true` helper never stops.

The fix is to re-hire the helper as a **native sidecar**: move it into `initContainers` with the badge `restartPolicy: Always`. Native sidecars are special — when the worker (the real `containers:` entry) finishes, Kubernetes **automatically shuts off** the sidecar. Faucet off, room empties, chore checked off. Job **Complete**.

One catch: you can't just tweak the helper in place. A Job's pod template is **frozen** once created — so you **delete** the Job and **recreate** it with the helper in the right spot.

**Watch out for:**

- **A Job completes only when every `containers:` entry exits.** A forever-loop helper in `containers:` blocks completion. Move it to `initContainers` + `restartPolicy: Always`.
- **Don't try to `kubectl edit` the running Job's containers** — the pod template is immutable. `delete` then recreate.
- **Keep `restartPolicy: Never` (or `OnFailure`) at the pod level** for Jobs — that's separate from the sidecar's own `restartPolicy: Always`.
- The worker stays in the normal `containers:` list; only the long-running helper becomes the sidecar.
questions.deepDive:
## Fixing a Job that never completes (sidecar) — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
A **Job completes only when all its `containers:` terminate successfully.** A long-running helper in `containers:` never exits, so the pod stays `Running` and the Job hangs. Make the helper a **native sidecar** (`initContainers` + `restartPolicy: Always`) and the kubelet tears it down automatically once the worker finishes — so the Job completes.

### Why the plain sidecar breaks the Job
| Container placement | Does it block Job completion? |
|---|---|
| Worker in `containers:`, exits | No — it's supposed to exit |
| Helper in `containers:`, `while true` | **Yes** — Job waits for it forever |
| Helper in `initContainers:` + `restartPolicy: Always` | **No** — native sidecar is terminated when the worker exits |

A Job's success is defined by its pods reaching a terminal **Succeeded** phase, which requires **every** main container to have exited. Native sidecars are explicitly excluded from this wait — the kubelet sends them SIGTERM after the last main container finishes.

### The fix, step by step
Job pod templates are **immutable**, so you can't edit the containers of a running Job. Delete and recreate:

```bash
kubectl -n sidecar-learn delete job batch-job --ignore-not-found
```
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: batch-job
  namespace: sidecar-learn
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never          # pod-level: Never or OnFailure for Jobs
      initContainers:
      - name: helper
        image: busybox:1.36
        restartPolicy: Always        # <-- makes helper a native sidecar
        command: ["sh","-c","while true; do echo helping; sleep 5; done"]
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh","-c","echo working; sleep 5; echo done"]
```
```bash
kubectl -n sidecar-learn wait --for=condition=complete job/batch-job --timeout=90s
```

### Two different restartPolicy fields — don't confuse them
| Field | Scope | Valid values | Role here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.template.spec.restartPolicy` | **pod-level** | `Never`, `OnFailure` (Jobs) | How the Job retries failed pods |
| `initContainers[].restartPolicy` | **container-level** | `Always` (for sidecar) | Turns the init container into a native sidecar |

A Job's pod-level `restartPolicy` may **not** be `Always` — but the sidecar's own container-level `restartPolicy: Always` is required and is a separate setting.

### Verify
```bash
# Job completed?
kubectl -n sidecar-learn get job batch-job
kubectl -n sidecar-learn get job batch-job -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Complete")].status}'; echo  # True

# helper really is a native sidecar?
kubectl -n sidecar-learn get job batch-job \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].name}:{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[0].restartPolicy}'; echo  # helper:Always
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Editing the live Job fails** — pod template is immutable; `delete` then recreate.
- **Leaving the helper in `containers:`** keeps the Job hanging no matter what else you change.
- **Forgetting `restartPolicy: Always`** on the helper makes it an ordinary init container that must exit first — with a `while true` command the Job's pods get stuck in `Init` and never even start the worker.
- **Pod-level `restartPolicy: Always`** is rejected for Jobs — keep it `Never`/`OnFailure`.
- Completed Jobs linger unless you set `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` — not required here but good to know.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n <ns> delete job <name> --ignore-not-found
# recreate: helper -> initContainers + restartPolicy: Always ; worker -> containers
kubectl -n <ns> wait --for=condition=complete job/<name> --timeout=90s
```
